# ADR 0001 — Transcription engine: faster-whisper `tiny.en`

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-08-01
**Phase:** 1 (PRD §9)
**Supersedes:** the latency-only selection recorded in `docs/gates/probe.md`
**Measurement:** `docs/adr/0001-engine-selection.bench.md` (generated by
`scripts/bench_engines.py --runs 9 --trim`)

---

## Decision

**faster-whisper (CTranslate2), model `tiny.en`, `int8`, `beam_size = 1`, with
silence trimming applied in `audio/vad.py` rather than by the engine.**

Moonshine was benchmarked as PRD §7.2 and §9 require. It is **not** selected,
and the reason is not the one the numbers first suggest.

## Context

PRD §7.2 already named `tiny.en` on 2026-07-31 (objection A3), replacing
`base.en`. But that selection was made on **latency alone**, and §7.2 says so
in the same breath:

> This table still selects on latency alone, and `tiny.en` has the worst
> accuracy of the candidates. [...] **Do not finalise the model choice until
> the Phase 1 corpus exists** (objection O7).

The corpus now exists — six desk-mic samples, 111.6 s, 264 reference words,
transcripts committed and audio deliberately not (`.gitignore`). Two things
were also wrong with the earlier evidence and are fixed here:

1. **Moonshine had never been benchmarked**, despite §7.2 requiring it. It was
   the stated reason `TranscriptionEngine` is an ABC rather than a module of
   functions, so an unmeasured Moonshine left the project's main extension
   point justified by a guess.
2. **Trimming was applied by faster-whisper's own `vad_filter`**, which
   Moonshine has no equivalent of. A comparison run that way measures the
   trimmer. Every figure below uses one trimmer — the product's
   `VoiceActivityDetector` — applied once per sample, outside the timed region,
   identically to every engine.

## What was measured

Apple M3 Max (10 performance / 4 efficiency cores), macOS 27.0, CPython 3.14.5,
faster-whisper 1.2.1, CTranslate2 4.8.1, `useful-moonshine-onnx` 20251121.
`cpu_threads = 10` (`hw.perflevel0.physicalcpu`). 54 observations per model
(6 samples × 9 timed runs, one warm-up discarded). Nearest-rank percentiles.

### Latency — transcription only, and therefore a floor

| Model | p50 | p95 | vs G1 (400 / 800 ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `moonshine/tiny` | **163 ms** | **233 ms** | PASS |
| **`tiny.en`** | **278 ms** | **421 ms** | **PASS** |
| `moonshine/base` | 280 ms | 428 ms | PASS |
| `base.en` | 489 ms | 867 ms | MISS |
| `distil-small.en` | 751 ms | 828 ms | MISS |
| `small.en` | 1,146 ms | 2,986 ms | MISS |
| `distil-large-v3` | 2,595 ms | 2,879 ms | MISS (also misses G1-CPU) |

`postprocess` and `inject` do not exist yet, so these are floors and G1 has
less headroom than the table implies. `base.en` misses **p95** at 867 ms before
either of those stages is built — the elimination that §7.2 made on a p50 is
confirmed here on the half of G1 that matters more.

### Accuracy — relative comparison only, not a G2 measurement

Macro-average, per PRD §7.2 as amended under objection A3. The per-sample range
is shown because a mean of six numbers hides which sample moved it.

| Model | WER (macro) | Per-sample range | Substitutions | Deletions | Insertions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `small.en` | 5.76% | 0.0–19.1% | 11 | 2 | 5 |
| `distil-large-v3` | 6.75% | 0.0–17.0% | 12 | 3 | 6 |
| `distil-small.en` | 10.57% | 0.0–24.1% | 14 | 3 | 10 |
| `base.en` | 11.41% | 0.0–27.7% | 18 | 7 | 9 |
| **`tiny.en`** | **19.33%** | 2.0–42.9% | 25 | **4** | 10 |
| `moonshine/base` | 23.93% | 0.0–71.4% | 20 | **14** | 8 |
| `moonshine/tiny` | 27.32% | 3.3–71.4% | 29 | **12** | 11 |

**Every pair involving `tiny.en` is statistically indistinguishable on this
corpus** — all 95% Wilson intervals overlap, and the true intervals are wider
still because word errors cluster within an utterance. One misrecognised word
moves the micro figure by 0.38 points. This corpus can eliminate; it cannot
rank.

## Why `tiny.en` and not `moonshine/tiny`

`moonshine/tiny` is the fastest thing measured — 163 ms p50 against 278 ms,
115 ms of headroom that Phase 2a and Phase 3 would be glad of. Three arguments
against it, in ascending order of how much they should count.

**1. The dependency cost is disproportionate.** `useful-moonshine-onnx` pulls
librosa, numba, scipy and scikit-learn. faster-whisper is required regardless
— the Silero VAD weights that `audio/vad.py` loads ship *inside* the
faster-whisper wheel, and that is a G3 requirement, not a convenience (a VAD
that downloaded its own weights would fire exactly the runtime fetch this
project gates on). Selecting Moonshine means shipping both runtimes or giving
up the bundled VAD asset.

**2. The unmeasured tiers only exist for one of them.** §7.2's `model = "auto"`
table has CUDA rows. They are labelled estimates and no v1 user reaches them
(§3 makes macOS the only platform), but faster-whisper spans CPU and CUDA from
one API and Moonshine does not. Weak, and listed for completeness.

**3. Moonshine's errors are the wrong *kind*, and this survives the statistics.**
This is the argument that decides it. The rate comparison is not available —
the Wilson intervals overlap and this ADR will not rank on a difference the
corpus cannot see. But the **error breakdown** is a different claim. Moonshine
deletes 12–14 words where the faster-whisper models delete 2–7; roughly three
times the deletion rate, and `moonshine/base` deletes more than
`moonshine/tiny` despite being the larger model. Both Moonshine rows have a
per-sample worst case of 71.4%.

For a dictation product those failures are not equivalent. A substituted word
is wrong on screen and the user fixes it. A deleted word is **silent data
loss** — the user has to notice an absence, in text they just dictated and have
not read yet. PRD §8's persist-before-inject exists because losing the user's
words is the failure this product refuses to have, and an engine whose
characteristic error is dropping them is the wrong instrument for that
principle, independent of where its WER lands.

That argument is about failure mode, not rate, so the CI overlap does not
touch it. It is also the honest reason: with rates indistinguishable, the
decision had to rest on something else, and this is what it rested on.

## Alternatives considered and rejected

| Candidate | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| `moonshine/tiny` | See above. **Reconsider if G1 headroom becomes binding** once post-processing and injection land — it buys 115 ms p50, which is more than the ~50 ms §7.2 budgeted for both remaining stages. |
| `moonshine/base` | Dominated. Same p50 as `tiny.en` (280 vs 278 ms), same p95 (428 vs 421 ms), worse macro WER (23.93% vs 19.33%), and the deletion problem is worse than `moonshine/tiny`'s. No axis on which it wins. |
| `base.en` | Misses G1's p95 at 867 ms with nothing built downstream of it. Better accuracy (11.41%) but there is no budget to spend on it. |
| `distil-small.en`, `small.en` | 751 ms and 1,146 ms p50. `small.en`'s p95 of 2,986 ms is the repetition-loop excursion this project documents as its failure mode. |
| `distil-large-v3` | 2,595 ms p50. §7.2's original Apple Silicon selection, wrong by roughly 7×, and the only candidate that also misses G1-CPU. Kept in the table so the ADR shows the row it rejects rather than asserting it. |

## Consequences

**Accepted, knowingly:** `tiny.en` has the worst accuracy of the
faster-whisper candidates, and the gap to `base.en` (19.33% vs 11.41% macro) is
large as a point estimate even though this corpus cannot certify it. The bet is
that PRD §7.5's post-processing chain closes part of that gap, and **that bet
is not yet tested** — PRD §9's Phase 5 is `UNRESOLVED, corpus-blocked`, and the
one experiment run so far made real ASR output 5–28× *worse*. If Phase 3's edit
rate (G2) comes back bad, this ADR is the thing to revisit first, and the
revisit has a name: `base.en` plus whatever latency Phase 2a and 3 turn out not
to need.

**The tier is unaffected.** `tiny.en` measures p50 258 ms / p95 386 ms on the
install check's reference clip and 300 ms / 373 ms through the product path
over this corpus — Tier A on both, with the p95 inside 700 ms by a wide margin.

**`TranscriptionEngine` earns its ABC, on evidence rather than assertion.**
Moonshine is a real alternative that a real measurement declined for a stated
reason, and the reason (deletion-heavy failure) is one that a different corpus
or a newer release could overturn. That is exactly the condition §6.3 sets for
a replacement boundary.

## What this does not establish

- **One speaker, one microphone, one room.** A model that wins here has won on
  one voice. Not fixable by running the benchmark again.
- **Mean sample duration is 18.6 s**, not the 10 s G1 is defined against. Whisper
  pads to a 30 s encoder window regardless, so this matters less than the ratio
  suggests, and it biases *against* the selected model rather than for it.
- **WER is not perfectly reproducible.** Two runs of this script over identical
  input returned 7.20% and 6.82% micro for `small.en` — greedy decoding is not
  bit-deterministic across threaded CTranslate2 runs. The variation is smaller
  than any gap this ADR relies on, but a future comparison inside 0.4 points
  cannot be trusted without repeats.
- **Macro-average is sensitive to the short sample.** `06-short` has 7
  reference words, so three errors on it is 42.9% and it carries the same
  weight as a 60-word sample. `tiny.en`'s 19.33% macro is substantially that
  one sample. Macro is still the right choice for the reason §7.2 gives — each
  sample is one dictation event, and the user experiences them one at a time —
  but the corpus should grow a second short sample before anyone reads a macro
  difference as an engine difference.
- **Edit rate (G2) is untouched.** That is Phase 3, and it is the actual
  product goal.
